title: A Step toward Stateful HW-SW Migration: An Architecture-agnostic Checkpointing-rollback Toolchain
authors: Maxime France-Pillois; Zihan Huang; Jiaxun Yang; Edson Horta; Binoy Ravindran; Antonio Barbalace
motivating_problem: Move stateful work between unlike hardware and software targets without losing live execution state.
general_principle: Instrument a target-independent IR with explicit equivalence points and generate target-specific checkpoint/restore code.
proof_or_performance_argument: Mechanism and recovery semantics are argued through compiler instrumentation and controlled output commits; evaluation measures toolchain behavior.
practical_connection: FPGA-to-CPU checkpoint and rollback with explicit restrictions on restorable call depth.
evaluation_breadth: Multiple applications and target paths; compiler and runtime measurements.
artifact_strength: Concrete toolchain and generated code; no artifact bytes redistributed here.
narrative_sequence: Migration problem -> IR equivalence mechanism -> implementation -> experiments -> limitations.
section_pattern: Introduction; background; design; implementation; evaluation; related work; conclusion.
figure_table_roles: Pipeline and checkpoint placement diagrams; evaluation tables/plots.
delta_to_this_work: Supplies concrete state-equivalence machinery that this project assumes. It does not characterize least pending-work drains under fixed FIFO capacities.
checked_pages_or_sections: Complete 26-page text; architecture, Sections 4.1-4.2, figures, evaluation, limitations.
access_notes: Author-posted/publisher-indexed full text inspected; DOI metadata cross-checked.
